# standard-application-engineering

<!-- generated by standards.py from projectious-work/standards; do not edit -->

Binding company standard. The rules below are the summary; the linked file is authoritative. Read only the section the task needs.

## Application profiles for engineering standards

Select standards by product behavior, not implementation language. Declare
every applicable profile, combine their requirements, and make exceptions
explicit and reviewable. Services, workers, and remote MCP servers follow
*Twelve-Factor App* with the listed deviations: layered CLI configuration,
local release, development containers, and evidence as a separate channel.

- Twelve-Factor alignment
- Conditional overlays
- Composite products
- Applicability record

## Command-line interface design standard

Each CLI picks one recorded style (ADR): A Unix utility `tool [opts]
[operands]`, B verb–resource `tool <verb> <type> [<name>]` (kubectl), or C
object–action `tool <object> <action>` (OpenStackClient). All follow the
*Unix Philosophy* and the baseline: `--help` with examples, `--version`,
long names for all options, `--` and `-`, machine envelope as contract, no
secrets in options, prompts only on a TTY, `--dry-run` for destructive use.

Full standard: `.standards/command-line-interface-design.md`. Sections:

- Purpose and scope
- Choosing a style
- Baseline for every style
- A. Unix utility style
- B. Verb–resource style (kubectl)
- C. Object–action style (OpenStackClient)

## Application configuration standard

Configuration precedence answers which source wins; authority answers
whether that source may set the key at all. Preserve both, expose redacted
provenance, and never use committed project configuration as an implicit
privilege escalation path. Services and workers are environment-first
(*Twelve-Factor App* III); layered files are for CLIs.

Full standard: `.standards/application-configuration.md`. Sections:

- Purpose and scope
- Precedence
- Authority is separate from precedence
- File and value behavior
- Effective configuration and provenance
- Testing

## Application output, logging, and evidence standard

Output answers the request. Logs are a disposable event stream that explains
operation (*Twelve-Factor App* XI). Evidence is a durable record written on
purpose that must survive log loss; a log line is never proof. Do not collapse
these channels. Structure and redact events before rendering or export.

Full standard: `.standards/application-output-logging-and-evidence.md`. Sections:

- Purpose and scope
- Three information channels
- Semantic events and rendering
- Streams and formats
- Redaction and data handling
- Failure and correlation
- Evidence integrity
- Testing

## Compatibility and machine-interface standard

Treat public and persisted machine interfaces as products. Version their
meaning, keep human rendering separate, prove rejection behavior, and never
call a change compatible based only on syntactic schema compatibility.

Full standard: `.standards/compatibility-and-machine-interfaces.md`. Sections:

- Purpose and scope
- Versioning
- Machine-readable results
- CLI profile
- Change classification
- Contract verification
